subproblem.title: Mass of an integer multiplicity current: M_W(τ(M, θ, ξ)) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n (Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3))
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and let the IMRep R = (C, θ, ξ) in U represent T ∈ 𝒟_n(U). Then for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, M_W(T) = R.measure(W) = ∫_{C∩W} θ dH^n, where M_W(T) is Simon's mass (6.2.5) with the Euclidean coefficient norm |·|_E on n-covectors (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–766, stated there without proof), Definition 3.1 (lines 733–753) and the mass (6.2.4)–(6.2.8). Notation: Λ^n is the space of n-covectors (continuous alternating n-forms on ℝ^P); for α ∈ Λ^n, |α|_E := (Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})²)^{1/2} (covectorEuclideanNorm); ev_τ(α) := α(τ_1, …, τ_n); μ := R.measure = θ H^n⌞C. A form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) is admissible if tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(z)|_E ≤ 1 for all z, and M_W(T) = sup ofReal T(ω) over admissible ω.

0. (Reduction and conventions.) Test forms in U have tsupport ⊆ U and C ⊆ U, so M_W(T) and μ(W) do not change if W is replaced by the open set W ∩ U. Assume W ⊆ U. All masses and measures are compared in [0, ∞]. The map α ↦ (α(e_I))_{I strictly increasing} is an injective linear map from Λ^n into a Euclidean space (an alternating n-form is determined by its values on increasing coordinate tuples), so |·|_E is the norm of an inner product on Λ^n; in particular its closed unit ball B_E is convex and the radial retraction onto B_E is 1-Lipschitz for |·|_E.

1. (Multilinear algebra.) (a) For every orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) in ℝ^P and α ∈ Λ^n, |α(τ)| ≤ |α|_E. (b) For every such τ there is β_τ ∈ Λ^n with |β_τ|_E = 1 and β_τ(τ) = 1.
 Proof. For an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P put S_f(α) := Σ_{(j_1,…,j_n) ∈ {1,…,P}^n} α(f_{j_1}, …, f_{j_n})². (i) S_f(α) does not depend on f: change the basis in one slot at a time; with the other slots fixed, v ↦ α(…, v, …) is a linear functional λ and Σ_i λ(f_i)² = |λ|² = Σ_i λ(e_i)² (Parseval). (ii) S_e(α) = n! |α|_E²: index tuples with a repeated index contribute 0 (α is alternating), and each strictly increasing I is obtained from exactly n! injective tuples, each contributing α(e_I)². For (a), extend τ to an orthonormal basis f with f_i = τ_i (i ≤ n); then n! |α|_E² = S_f(α) ≥ Σ_{σ∈Sym(n)} α(τ_{σ(1)}, …, τ_{σ(n)})² = n! α(τ)². For (b), let β_τ(v_1, …, v_n) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j=1..n} (the wedge of the covectors ⟨τ_i, ·⟩; SimonGMT Chapter06.wedgeCovectors_apply_det), an alternating n-form with β_τ(τ) = det I = 1. For the basis f above, β_τ(f_{j_1}, …, f_{j_n}) = ±1 if (j_1, …, j_n) is a permutation of (1, …, n) and 0 otherwise (a zero column if some j_k > n, two equal columns if an index repeats); so S_f(β_τ) = n! and |β_τ|_E = 1.
 Consequence: by the orientation condition of R, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ C we have ξ(x) = ±ev_τ for an orthonormal n-frame τ, hence |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α|_E for all α, and ξ(x)(±β_τ) = 1 with |±β_τ|_E = 1; that is, sup{ξ(x)(β) : |β|_E ≤ 1} = 1.

2. (M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).) If μ(W) = ∞ there is nothing to prove. Let ω be admissible. As tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, |θ ξ(ω)| ≤ θ 1_{tsupport ω} H^n-a.e. on C is integrable, and θ ξ(ω) vanishes off W. Hence T(ω) = R.action ω = ∫_C θ ξ(ω) dH^n ≤ ∫_{C∩W} θ |ξ(ω)| dH^n ≤ ∫_{C∩W} θ dH^n = μ(W). Taking the supremum over admissible ω, M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).

3. (M_W(T) ≥ μ(W).) Fix a real t < μ(W) and η ∈ (0, 1). If W ≠ ℝ^P let K_j := {z : |z| ≤ j, dist(z, ℝ^P ∖ W) ≥ 1/j} and O_j := {z : |z| < j + 1, dist(z, ℝ^P ∖ W) > 1/(2j)}; if W = ℝ^P let K_j := closedBall(0, j) and O_j := ball(0, j + 1). The K_j are compact and increase to W, so μ(K) > t for K := K_j with j large; put O := O_j. Then O is open, K ⊆ O, and closure(O) is a compact subset of W ⊆ U, so μ(K) ≤ μ(O) < ∞.
 3.1 (A Borel near-maximizing covector field.) Let ξ̃ be a Borel function with ξ̃ = ξ H^n-a.e. on C, and let {β_k}_{k≥1} be a countable dense subset of B_E := {β ∈ Λ^n : |β|_E ≤ 1}. By step 1 and the continuity of the linear map ξ̃(x), sup_k ξ̃(x)(β_k) = 1 for H^n-a.e. x ∈ C. Define recursively A_k := {x ∈ C ∩ K : ξ̃(x)(β_k) > 1 − η} ∖ ⋃_{i<k} A_i (disjoint Borel sets; (C ∩ K) ∖ ⋃_k A_k is H^n-null) and g := Σ_k 1_{A_k} β_k. Then g is Borel, |g|_E ≤ 1, g = 0 off K, and ξ(x)(g(x)) ≥ 1 − η for H^n-a.e. x ∈ C ∩ K; hence ∫_C θ ξ(g) dH^n ≥ (1 − η) μ(K).
 3.2 (Smooth admissible approximation.) ν := μ⌞O is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P (a Radon measure). By density of continuous compactly supported functions in L¹ of the finite (hence regular) Borel measure ν on ℝ^P, applied to the coordinates of g in a basis of Λ^n, there is a continuous compactly supported g₀ : ℝ^P → Λ^n with ∫ |g₀ − g|_E dν < η. Let χ ∈ C_c(O) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and χ = 1 on K, and g₁ := χ g₀; since g = χ g (g = 0 off K), |g₁ − g|_E = χ |g₀ − g|_E ≤ |g₀ − g|_E, so g₁ is continuous with compact support in O and ∫ |g₁ − g|_E dν < η. Let π(v) := v / max(1, |v|_E) be the radial retraction onto B_E; it is 1-Lipschitz for the inner-product norm |·|_E (step 0) and fixes B_E, so g₂ := π ∘ g₁ is continuous with compact support in O, |g₂|_E ≤ 1 and |g₂ − g|_E ≤ |g₁ − g|_E pointwise. Mollify: h := g₂ * φ_ε (coordinatewise convolution with a mollifier φ_ε ≥ 0, ∫ φ_ε = 1, spt φ_ε ⊆ B_ε(0)), where ε < dist(spt g₂, ℝ^P ∖ O) is so small that sup_z |h(z) − g₂(z)|_E ≤ η/(1 + ν(ℝ^P)) (uniform continuity of g₂). Then h is C^∞ with compact tsupport h ⊆ O ⊆ W ⊆ U, and |h(z)|_E ≤ 1 for all z, since h(z) is an average of values of g₂ in the convex set B_E. Thus h is admissible for M_W(T), and ∫ |h − g|_E dν ≤ 2η.
 3.3 (Estimate.) h − g vanishes off O and |ξ(x)(v)| ≤ |v|_E for H^n-a.e. x ∈ C (step 1), so |T(h) − ∫_C θ ξ(g) dH^n| = |∫_C θ ξ(h − g) dH^n| ≤ ∫ |h − g|_E dν ≤ 2η. Therefore M_W(T) ≥ ofReal T(h) ≥ ofReal((1 − η) μ(K) − 2η) ≥ ofReal((1 − η) t − 2η) (μ(K) is finite). Letting η ↓ 0 and then t ↑ μ(W) (through real values; if μ(W) = ∞, t → ∞) gives M_W(T) ≥ μ(W).

4. By steps 2 and 3, T.massOn W = R.measure W for every open W.
proof_key_steps: Parseval in each slot shows the Euclidean coefficient norm is basis independent; hence |α(τ)| ≤ |α|_E and the wedge β_τ of the dual frame has |β_τ|_E = 1 and β_τ(τ) = 1.
Upper bound: T(ω) = ∫_C θ ξ(ω) ≤ ∫_{C∩W} θ dH^n for admissible ω.
Lower bound: a Borel near-maximizing covector field on a compact K ⊆ W, approximated in L¹(θH^n⌞C) by smooth admissible forms (density of C_c, radial retraction, mollification).

audit.reason: Slotwise Parseval and determinant covectors establish the correct coefficient-norm normalization. The upper estimate and smooth, norm-preserving L1 approximation establish equality for every open W, including infinite mass.
